After a two-year gap, Apple is developing a new iMac powered by the M6 chip and a fresh lineup of colours, according to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, with the machine expected to go on sale by the end of the year.

The iMac has never had a particularly frequent refresh cycle, having skipped both the M2 and M5 chip generations, while a larger-screen variant has never materialised — largely because Apple has continued steering them toward the Mac Studio or a Mac mini paired with a Studio Display. That said, Apple is now preparing to unveil a new iMac with the M6 chip.

Gurman notes that this update will bring "multiple new colours," though he offers no further detail. The 2024 M4 model only made minor adjustments to the palette, retaining the original seven colours with subtle tonal shifts. The new iMac is likewise expected to go on sale sometime this year.

This means the upcoming autumn could be a significant quarter for Apple's Mac lineup. Beyond the likely M6-powered iMac, the lineup is also expected to include: a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen and tandem OLED, a new 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6, and new Mac Studio models featuring the M5 Max and M5 Ultra (subject to supply). New Mac minis with the M6 and M5 Pro could also make an appearance, though they are expected to arrive a little later.

Apple's M6 chip will be the first Mac processor built on the new 2nm process, but reportedly there will be no M6 Pro, M6 Max, or M6 Ultra variants, as Apple plans to accelerate the rollout of the M7 series.
